title: Hyderabad State
capsule: Hyderabad State was the largest of British India's princely states, founded in 1724 when Asaf Jah I (Nizam ul-Mulk Chin Qilich Khan) was appointed viceroy of the Deccan and then asserted effective independence from the declining Mughal empire. At its greatest extent the state covered roughly 82,000 square miles encompassing most of the Deccan Plateau, with Hyderabad city as its capital and Urdu as the court language; its rulers, the Nizams, were reputed to be among the wealthiest individuals in the world in the early twentieth century. The seventh and last Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan, declined to join the Indian Union at independence in 1947; the Indian Army launched Operation Polo (September 1948), defeating the state's forces within five days, and Hyderabad was absorbed into India.
